rules: When a trap is taken into M-mode, the mstatus (or mstatush) field MPV is set to the value of the virtualization mode V at the time of the trap.
When a trap is taken into M-mode, the mstatus (or mstatush) field MPP is set to the nominal privilege mode at the time of the trap.
When an MRET instruction is executed, the virtualization mode V is set to the value of mstatus (or mstatush) field MPV, unless mstatus (or mstatush) field MPP is 3, in which case V remains 0.

When a trap is taken into M-mode, the mstatus (or mstatush) field GVA is set to 1 for any trap that writes a guest virtual address to mtval (breakpoint, address misaligned, access fault, page fault, or guest-page fault).
When a trap is taken into M-mode, the mstatus (or mstatush) field GVA is set to 0 for any trap other than those that write a guest virtual address to mtval.
When the hart is in HS-mode, mstatus field TVM=1 prevents access to hgatp or execution of HFENCE.GVMA or HINVAL.GVMA.
When the hart is in HS-mode, mstatus field TVM=1 has no effect on accesses to vsatp or instructions HFENCE.VVMA or HINVAL.VVMA.
When mstatus field MPRV=0, translation and protection for explicit memory accesses behave as normal.
When mstatus field MPRV=1 and mstatus field MPV=0 and mstatus field MPP=0, explicit memory accesses are translated and protected as U-level access with HS-level translation and protection only.
When mstatus field MPRV=1 and mstatus field MPV=0 and mstatus field MPP=1, explicit memory accesses are translated and protected as HS-level access with HS-level translation and protection only.
When mstatus field MPRV=1 and mstatus field MPP=3, explicit memory accesses are translated and protected as M-level access with no translation.
When mstatus field MPRV=1 and mstatus field MPV=1 and mstatus field MPP=0, explicit memory accesses are translated and protected as VU-level access with two-stage translation and protection.

When mstatus field MPRV=1 and mstatus field MPV=1 and mstatus field MPP=1, explicit memory accesses are translated and protected as VS-level access with two-stage translation and protection, and vsstatus.SUM applies instead of the HS-level SUM bit.
When a trap is taken into M-mode, the mstatus (or mstatush) fields MPIE and MIE are written.
When an MRET instruction is executed, mstatus (or mstatush) field MPV is set to 0.
When an MRET instruction is executed, mstatus (or mstatush) field MPP is set to 0.
When an MRET instruction is executed, mstatus (or mstatush) field MIE is set to the value of MPIE.
When an MRET instruction is executed, mstatus (or mstatush) field MPIE is set to 1.
When a trap is taken into privilege mode x, the xPELP bit in mstatus is set to ELP and ELP is set to NO_LP_EXPECTED.
When an MRET instruction is executed and the new privilege mode is y, ELP is set to the value of MPELP in mstatus if yLPE is 1.
When an MRET instruction is executed and the new privilege mode is y, ELP is set to NO_LP_EXPECTED if yLPE is 0.
When an MRET instruction is executed, the MPELP bit in mstatus is set to NO_LP_EXPECTED.
When an SRET instruction is executed and the new privilege mode is y, ELP is set to the value of SPELP in mstatus if yLPE is 1.
When an SRET instruction is executed and the new privilege mode is y, ELP is set to NO_LP_EXPECTED if yLPE is 0.
When an SRET instruction is executed, the SPELP bit in mstatus is set to NO_LP_EXPECTED.
